Get Treasury Yield Curve Data from FRED

Source: R/data-utils.r
get_treasury_yield_data.Rd

Downloads U.S. Treasury yield curve data from FRED API for multiple maturities and processes it into a consistent format suitable for DNS model calibration.

Usage

get_treasury_yield_data(
  api_key = NULL,
  maturities = c("1MO", "3MO", "6MO", "1", "2", "3", "5", "7", "10", "20", "30"),
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL,
  convert_to_decimal = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  fill_missing = TRUE,
  max_gap = Inf,
  date_order = c("descending", "ascending"),
  retries = 3L,
  cache_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

api_key

Character. FRED API key. If NULL, will look for fred_api_key environment variable.

maturities

Character vector. Maturities to download. Options are "1MO", "2MO", "3MO", "6MO", "1", "2", "3", "5", "7", "10", "20", "30".

start_date

Date or character in "YYYY-MM-DD" format. The earliest date to include.

end_date

Date or character in "YYYY-MM-DD" format. The latest date to include.

convert_to_decimal

Logical. If TRUE, convert yields from percentages to decimal format.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print processing information.

fill_missing

Logical, or one of "forward" / "none". If TRUE (the default) gaps are filled by carrying the last observation forward in calendar time.

max_gap

Numeric. Maximum number of calendar days a value may be carried across when fill_missing is in effect. Gaps wider than this are left as NA. Defaults to Inf, which fills every gap.

date_order

Character. Row order of the returned frame: "descending" (the default, most recent first) or "ascending".

retries

Integer. HTTP attempts per series, passed to fetch_fred_series.

cache_dir

Character. Directory in which to cache responses, passed to fetch_fred_series. NULL disables caching.

Value

A data.frame with processed yield curve data where:

  • The first column is 'Date' containing the observation dates.

  • Subsequent columns contain yield values for different maturities.

  • Column names represent maturities in years.

Details

This function fetches data from FRED for the following series:

  • DGS1MO (1-Month)

  • DGS3MO (3-Month)

  • DGS6MO (6-Month)

  • DGS1 (1-Year)

  • DGS2 (2-Year)

  • DGS3 (3-Year)

  • DGS5 (5-Year)

  • DGS7 (7-Year)

  • DGS10 (10-Year)

  • DGS20 (20-Year)

  • DGS30 (30-Year)

Requires a FRED API key which can be obtained free at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/api_key.html

Gap filling runs on an ascending date index, so a missing yield takes the value of the most recent earlier observation. This matters because the frame is returned newest-first: filling in row order would carry values backwards in time and introduce look-ahead bias into anything calibrated on the result. Long series have genuine multi-year holes (DGS20 before 1993, DGS30 between 2002 and 2006); set max_gap to stop those being bridged.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Set your API key first
Sys.setenv(fred_api_key = "your_api_key_here")
yield_data <- get_treasury_yield_data(start_date = "2020-01-01")
head(yield_data)
} # }
